title: Meridian Health - On-prem/Airgapped Deployment Discovery
summary: Initial discovery for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment of Redwood for Meridian Health. Discussed regulatory constraints (HIPAA), secure update/air gap process, hardware constraints (no internet, limited GPU options), KMS/HSM, RBAC/SSO, and benchmark/POC next steps.
topics: Air-gapped deployment model and update process
Hardware sizing and GPU constraints (A100 vs H100 vs T4 alternatives)
Encryption, KMS/HSM and key management in air-gapped env
Connectivity constraints and approved jumpbox strategy
next_steps: Redwood: send security packet and SOC2/ISO docs (Jill) by 2026-03-24
Redwood: propose hardware BOM + perf expectations (Samir) by 2026-03-25
Meridian: share network diagram and air-gapped jumpbox policy (Marcus) by 2026-03-26
Schedule on-site/virtual POC kickoff week of 2026-04-06
action_items: Samir Patel: produce draft hardware BOM and expected latency/throughput numbers by 2026-03-25
Jill Carter: send security/compliance packet, redacted logs examples by 2026-03-24
Marcus Lee: provide internal network diagram and list of approved USB/transfer procedures by 2026-03-26
Nadia Ortiz: compile compliance checklist (HIPAA controls) and circulate to Redwood by 2026-03-26
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jill Carter (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Alyssa Wong (Redwood SE), Dr. Emily Chen (CTO - Meridian), Marcus Lee (Cloud/Infra), Nadia Ortiz (Compliance), Alan Park (ML Lead)

[00:00] Jill Carter: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jill Carter from Redwood, i'm the a e on the account. we got Samir and Alyssa from eng here as well. emily, marcus, nadia, alan, thanks for taking the time.
[00:08] Dr. Emily Chen: hi, thanks for setting this up. we wanted to get a better idea of what an on-prem, air-gapped deployment would look like for us — given HIPAA and our internal policies.
[00:16] Jill Carter: absolutely. we'll run through high-level architecture, update/patch process for air-gapped sites, and then hardware sizing. samir, do you want to kick off with the architecture?
[00:23] Samir Patel: sure, yeah. so high level, the Redwood private control plane can be configured so that the management/control plane runs in a customer-managed VPC or completely on-prem. for air-gapped we support a sidecar update mechanism — the cluster doesn't need outbound internet. updates and model weights are delivered via signed packages that you validate with your HSM/KMS.
[00:41] Marcus Lee: ok, when you say signed packages, is that an over-the-wire signature check or do you verify on the host after we transfer files manually? we can't have any outbound checks from the cluster.
[00:50] Samir Patel: good question. it's designed for both: for fully air-gapped installs, we provide an offline package (tar.gz) signed with Redwood's code signing cert. the validation is local — the node's agent will check the signature using the public key you import into your HSM or local KMS. there is no call-home required.
[01:08] Nadia Ortiz: and from a compliance perspective, what about audit logs? we need immutable audit trails for config changes and access for at least seven years.
[01:15] Alyssa Wong: we generate operation logs and request-level audit logs. for private/on-prem installs those logs can be configured to ship to your SIEM. we also support locally-stored append-only logs and can provide signed log bundles for archival. i will flag that some of the logging metadata names might be different in the UI — sometimes the transcription shows 'KV cash' which is, sorry, 'KV cache' in the logs.
[01:36] Dr. Emily Chen: (laughs) yep we've seen the transcription quirks. alan — any immediate ML constraints we should flag?
[01:42] Alan Park: we're planning short sequences mostly — charting and notes summarization — but some of our models need prompt contexts up to 8k tokens. latency target is sub-200ms p95 on common inference paths. throughput: 200 concurrent requests during peak. we are also sensitive about model updates — we prefer to freeze a model for a month and only update after validation.
[02:03] Samir Patel: okay, two things there: kernel selection and batching will be tuned for your sequence distribution. for 8k tokens we typically recommend H100-class hardware for best latency, but with quantization we can get good perf on A100 or even some of the 80GB Ampere variants. for strict air-gapped low-internet shops, we can propose quantized variants that reduce memory footprint.
[02:27] Marcus Lee: our hardware constraint is we only have racks with A100 40GB and a couple of older T4 nodes. H100s are a stretch for budgeting. how does Redwood handle heterogeneous pools? can some requests go to smaller quantized models?
[02:40] Samir Patel: yes, smart routing can route by policy. you can define latency SLOs and cost tiers — requests that are tolerant to slightly higher latency can fall back to quantized model variants on A100 or even CPU for small requests. we also support model pinning per route so you can keep a strict production route pinned to a validated variant.
[02:59] Nadia Ortiz: for the sealed/offline updates: how are keys managed? we use an HSM with FIPS modules. we can't have Redwood hold any private keys.
[03:08] Samir Patel: absolutely. you bring your own KMS/HSM. during install you import Redwood's public signing key into your HSM. Your HSM verifies signatures for every package. Redwood never has access to customer private keys. we also support wrapping of model-encryption keys so that weights at rest are encrypted with customer-managed keys.
[03:26] Dr. Emily Chen: what about telemetry? we don't want telemetry flowing back to Redwood, even metrics.
[03:33] Jill Carter: that's fine. for private air-gapped installs telemetry is entirely optional. the control plane can run disconnected and we can ship an offline diagnostic bundle format that you send securely to your account team if you want help. no automatic call-home.
[03:46] Marcus Lee: another ops question: how do we apply emergency mitigations? say there's a critical CVE in a dependency, and we need a patch — what's the lead time to get a patch package and how do we validate it internally?
[03:56] Alyssa Wong: we maintain a security channel and will generate an emergency patch package. for air-gapped customers we typically provide an on-prem signed patch, with accompanying CVE notes and checksums. you validate via your HSM and apply. lead time depends on severity — for criticals we'd aim for 24-72 hours to produce a package, then it's your internal change control to apply.
[04:17] Nadia Ortiz: 24-72 hours is reasonable, but we need documented SLAs around providing mitigations and a process doc. can you share that?
[04:23] Jill Carter: yes, we'll include an incident response and emergency patching process in the security packet.
[04:28] [05:00] Marcus Lee: on networking, we plan to isolate the cluster in a restricted VLAN. we use a jumpbox pattern where vendors can SFTP artifacts into a staging host, then transfer to the cluster via controlled media. will Redwood support that approved jumpbox workflow and define expected artifact formats?
[05:16] Samir Patel: yes, that's exactly the pattern many customers use. we provide a signed package format and a short script to verify signatures and checksum. the script can run on the jumpbox or on an air-gapped host. we also support delivering Docker images as tarballs if you want to manage container runtime locally.
[05:32] Alan Park: on the model side — can we bring our own models, or do we have to use Redwood-verified models? we have internally trained models with PII patterns.
[05:41] Samir Patel: you can bring your own models. Redwood private supports model onboarding of customer weights. for air-gapped flows, you provide the model artifacts, we provide the loader and runtime integration. we do verification locally — we can provide a local release that validates model format, performs a quick signature check, and compiles optimized kernels.
[05:58] Dr. Emily Chen: anything about licensing? our legal team wants to avoid vendor code being installed with permissive exec rights — we need to audit runtime.
[06:07] Jill Carter: understood. we can provide the license and a list of runtime components, and we can run code scans and provide SBOMs (software bill of materials) for the packages.
[06:15] Nadia Ortiz: retention — logs with PHI must be kept only as long as necessary and be encrypted. can logs be redacted on-export?
[06:22] Alyssa Wong: yes, the logging framework supports redaction rules and field-level masking. you can configure it to never persist certain fields and to apply PII masks before writing to disk or export.
[06:33] [07:00] Marcus Lee: curious about perf: you mentioned quantization — how much performance loss should we expect with 4-bit quant vs fp16 on A100?
[07:11] Samir Patel: depends on model. for many decoder-only models, 4-bit quant can reduce memory by ~2-3x and can be within 5-15% latency increase, sometimes less if kernels are optimized. for p95 tail we recommend running a benchmark. we can simulate with your prompt set.
[07:28] Alan Park: can you run that benchmark against our sample dataset? we can provide 500 representative requests and some longer threads.
[07:35] Jill Carter: yes, that's standard. we'll run an on-prem benchmark during POC. for air-gapped customers we send a benchmark harness you run locally and share logs.
[07:45] Dr. Emily Chen: on security, is SSO supported? we use SAML with Okta.
[07:50] Samir Patel: yes — for private installs we support SAML/Okta integration and can map roles via SAML assertions. RBAC is configurable and you can integrate with your directory.
[07:58] Nadia Ortiz: and separation of duties? can we restrict admin access for model uploads vs infra ops?
[08:04] Alyssa Wong: yes, role definitions are separate. you can create a model-uploader role, an infra-admin role, and restrict access to model signing.
[08:11] Marcus Lee: any constraints on GPU drivers or container runtime — we run RHEL7 and have to stick to validated kernels.
[08:18] Samir Patel: we publish driver and runtime compatibility matrix. for some older OSes we provide validated container images and node-level configs. we'll include a compatibility doc in the packet.
[08:28] [09:00] Alan Park: about model updates: you mentioned a frozen cadence; how do we handle rollbacks if a new weights version degrades quality?
[09:06] Samir Patel: rollouts are versioned and we support canary routes and automatic rollback policies. in private installs, the control plane will let you define a canary percent and automatic metrics-based rollback. for air-gapped, the same logic runs locally — you just need to stage the release packages.
[09:22] Dr. Emily Chen: what's an expected POC scope and length for a health customer like us?
[09:27] Jill Carter: typically 4-6 weeks: week 0 install + validation, week 1-2 run benchmark and tuning, week 3 business validation (accuracy/regression tests), week 4 handoff and runbook. we can compress if you prefer.
[09:39] Marcus Lee: about cost: if we're buying dedicated capacity or private license, how does pricing change? is there an enterprise license for on-prem?
[09:46] Jill Carter: for private on-prem we offer an enterprise license + optional support tiers. pricing is a function of node count, support SLAs, and whether you want a maintenance + update bundle. we'll send a preliminary pricing sheet.
[09:58] Nadia Ortiz: the legal team will need indemnities around data handling and PHI. we can't have vendor processing logs off-site.
[10:05] Jill Carter: understood — we'll include data handling clauses in the enterprise agreement and make sure off-site telemetry is opt-in.
[10:11] [11:00] Marcus Lee: one more technical: KV cache persistence — if we restart nodes, how do you handle KV cache warmup? we want to avoid long warmup for large context sessions.
[11:20] Samir Patel: we have a persistent KV cache option where cache shards can be stored locally on fastest NVMe and replayed during restart. for air-gapped, you control the persistence policy. there is also a shared-cache mode across pool nodes if you accept an internal network overlay.
[11:40] Alan Park: that sounds useful — what's the storage requirement for a 8k-token model with 4 M active sessions?
[11:48] Samir Patel: rough back-of-envelope: depends on KV representation, but plan for 1-2GB per high-activity shard. we'll put numbers in the BOM Samir: (laughs) sorry, Samir repeated.
[11:59] [12:30] Dr. Emily Chen: let's talk stakeholders — who will be involved from your side during POC?
[12:36] Jill Carter: i will be primary commercial lead, samir and alyssa will be technical leads during the POC. we'll also include a dedicated customer success contact during onboarding.
[12:46] Nadia Ortiz: and from our side, marcus and alan will be tech leads, i'll handle compliance gating, emily will sponsor.
[12:53] Marcus Lee: can you share example architecture diagrams and an install playbook?
[12:58] Jill Carter: yes — next step we'll send security packet + install playbook + SBOM + compatibility matrix.
[13:05] [14:00] Alan Park: about Bring-Your-Own-Model (BYOM) — do you support quantize-on-load or do we have to provide pre-quantized weights?
[14:14] Samir Patel: we can support quantize-on-load in the runtime if you want — however for air-gapped we often prefer to provide a validated quantized artifact to minimize unknowns in your change window. we can do either.
[14:30] Marcus Lee: on the POC harness, you mentioned a script — does it produce perf traces we can ingest into our observability stack?
[14:38] Alyssa Wong: yes, the harness emits structured traces and token-level timings. for private installs you can configure exporters to push to your Prometheus/Elastic stack. if you want, we'll include a minimal adapter for your telemetry format.
[14:54] Dr. Emily Chen: are there any data residency issues with model provenance — we need to prove models were trained only on internal data for certain workloads.
[15:02] Samir Patel: that's more of a process/policy question — we can support BYOM and ensure provenance tags and model manifest metadata are stored locally. we also support adding provenance hashes to signatures so you can audit which dataset/version produced the model.
[15:18] Nadia Ortiz: can you provide sample manifest and signature format?
[15:22] Jill Carter: yes, included in the security packet.
[15:26] [16:00] Marcus Lee: on-node resource isolation — can we run Redwood runtime in a dedicated namespace and limit cgroups? we need to be able to memory- and cpu-isolate for multi-tenant cluster plans.
[16:13] Samir Patel: yes, we support namespace-based isolation and recommend using cgroups + node affinity. we also have a runtime mode for strict single-tenant GPU allocation.
[16:23] Alan Park: okay, last technical thing for now: model explainability — can you capture token salience or attention maps for auditing?
[16:31] Samir Patel: we can surface attention patterns and likelihood scores. for heavy instrumentation that's additional overhead but it's supported for audit runs.
[16:41] [17:00] Dr. Emily Chen: let's recap — main asks from us: show install playbook + security docs, sample manifest/signature, hardware BOM, benchmark harness, and pricing.
[17:09] Jill Carter: got it. from Redwood we'll deliver: security/compliance packet + install playbook + BOM + benchmark harness + license/pricing proposal. we'll aim to get those to you by 2026-03-25.
[17:18] Marcus Lee: timeline: after docs we'll try to schedule the POC for week of 2026-04-06.
[17:24] Nadia Ortiz: legal will need the data handling appendix — i'll reach back to specify any redlines after i review.
[17:30] Jill Carter: perfect. any other blockers?
[17:34] Alan Park: just the GPU procurement question — i'll follow up with a list of currently available nodes.
[17:38] Dr. Emily Chen: thanks everyone. this was helpful.
[17:41] Jill Carter: thanks all, we'll share notes and the packet.
[17:44] [18:00] -- brief dead air as folks drop --
[18:30] [47:30] Meeting end.
file_notes: Transcript retains informal speech patterns and occasional transcription errors (e.g., 'KV cash' vs KV cache). References to documents are placeholders; links will be shared via email.
